purpose: Turn the exploratory damping-scale solution into a precise central-circle normalization branch and identify the exact remaining lemma.

selected_branch.central_circle_identification: Lambda_eff^2 = lambda_S1 = 1/R1^2 up to a declared convention factor

key_observation.theta_bound_R1_le_2: Theta I contains R1 <= 2 as an admissibility bound.
key_observation.finite_count_implication: With C_Q=lambda_star=sigma_circle=1, N=64 gives R1 approximately 2.039, N=79 gives approximately 2.090, and N=448 gives approximately 2.471. These are close to but above the R1<=2 bound, so this naive finite-count epsilon is not a closed solution.
possible_repairs: derive epsilon_adm slightly smaller than 1/64 from basin separation
derive C_Q>1 or lambda_star>1 from the selected Hessian/semigroup
use the branch as a bound rather than equality

single_open_lemma.name: Selected Central-Circle Damping Identification Lemma
single_open_lemma.statement: The selected MTT/Strominger Hessian, semigroup bound, admissibility tolerance, and central-circle convention satisfy sigma_circle * sqrt(log(C_Q/epsilon_adm)/lambda_star) <= 2, with equality or a selected interior value fixed without target constants.
single_open_lemma.equivalent_output: A source-certified value or finite set for R1 independent of G_N, M_Pl, H0, rho_DE, and absolute f_a.
single_open_lemma.why_it_finishes_the_branch: Once R1 is selected, Theta IV already gives the Newton-structure factor 31.8 R1^3/G10; a separate action-normalization certificate for G10 would then determine G_N without backsolving.

closed_now: The algebraic damping-to-R1 branch is formulated.
The naive finite-count choices are tested and shown not to close the R1<=2 bound under sigma=C_Q=lambda_star=1.
The remaining obstruction is a single explicit lemma rather than an unstructured search.
forbidden_shortcuts: choose sigma_circle to force observed G_N
choose lambda_star after comparing to H0 or rho_DE
use observed target constants to select R1 or G10
